question: Assess whether the proposed mine closure plan creates apparent financial order by exporting irreversible consequence.

direct_observations: Downside risks of aquifer contamination are transferred to local farming cooperative.
Parent company liability terminates upon approval of the closure certificate.
contradictions: The proposal claims zero ecological footprint, but water monitoring sensors in Zone B are excluded.
counterevidence: Parent company agrees to fund a 2-year monitoring bond, although monitoring costs decay after year 2.
alternative_explanations: Limiting liability is a standard corporate governance mandate to attract investment.
Corporate restructuring may have legally partitioned liability prior to this specific closure proposal.
contradictions: Corporate sustainability reports claim 100% safety, whereas local geohydrology reports predict high-risk water table subsidence.
prohibited_conclusions: Do not declare the board members malicious.
Do not estimate hidden motives; evaluate only the liability-consequence partition.
